title: Khoresh gheymeh
subtitle: Persian split pea and lamb stew with fried potato
excerpt: Khoresh gheymeh is one of the most comforting stews in Persian cooking. Cubed lamb simmers with yellow split peas, dried limes, and turmeric into a thick, amber-coloured stew. The defining finish is a heap of thin fried potato matchsticks piled over each bowl. It is deeply savoury and warming.
sourceNotes: One of the most beloved Persian khoresh (stews). Dried limes (limu omani or loomi) give the stew its characteristic slightly smoky, fermented sourness. They are available in Persian and Middle Eastern grocers.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze without the fried potato. Make the potato fresh when serving.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The stew improves significantly the next day. Make up to 2 days ahead and refrigerate.

content.text: Khoresh gheymeh is named for the small cubes of lamb that give it its body. Yellow split peas dissolve partly into the stew, thickening it to something between a stew and a thick soup. Dried limes are pierced and added whole; they slowly release a deep, fermented sourness that anchors everything.
The fried potato on top is not decoration. It is an essential textural contrast: the stew is soft and giving, and the thin, crisp potato on top provides the crunch that makes each spoonful complete.

Dried limes (loomi or limu omani) are available in Iranian, Turkish, and Middle Eastern food shops. Pierce each one several times with a skewer or fork before adding; this allows the flavour to escape into the stew during cooking.

items.prepNote: to mimic dried lime sourness if loomi unavailable

content.text: Brown the lamb and build the stew

Melt the butter in a heavy casserole over medium-high heat. Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes until golden. Push aside and add the lamb cubes in batches, browning well on all sides, about 6 minutes per batch. Return all the lamb to the pot. Add the turmeric, cinnamon, and tomato puree and stir for 1 minute. Add the yellow split peas, stock, salt, and saffron water if using. Stir in the lemon juice or pierce the dried limes if using and nestle them in the pot. Bring to the boil.

Reduce the heat to a very gentle simmer, cover, and cook for 1 to 1.5 hours until the lamb is very tender and the split peas have softened and partially dissolved into the stew. The stew should be quite thick. Taste and adjust the salt. Add pomegranate syrup to balance if too heavy.

Cut the carrots into very thin matchstick strips, or use 2 medium potatoes instead. Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over high heat until very hot. Add the matchsticks in a thin layer, season with salt, and fry for 5 to 7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until golden and crisp. Drain on kitchen paper. Spoon the stew over rice and pile the fried potato on top.

rows.cause: Split peas did not dissolve as expected
rows.fix: Uncover and simmer on a slightly higher heat for 15 minutes to reduce. The split peas should dissolve enough to thicken the stew naturally.

rows.cause: Insufficient cooking time or heat too low
rows.fix: Continue simmering; lamb shoulder needs a full 90 minutes at a gentle but real simmer to become tender.

rows.cause: Oil not hot enough or potato too thick
rows.fix: Cut the potato very thin and make sure the oil is very hot before adding. Fry in batches if necessary.

content.text: Some versions include a small amount of pomegranate syrup stirred in at the end for a subtle sweet-sharp note. Replace the lamb with beef chuck if preferred. For a richer result, add a pinch of ground rose petals or advieh spice mix if you can find it.
The stew keeps for 3 days in the fridge and freezes for 3 months. The fried potato topping must be made fresh each time. Reheat gently on the hob with a splash of water to prevent sticking.

Khoresh gheymeh is one of the most popular everyday stews in Iran, served at family meals throughout the year. It is a common feature at religious gatherings, served in large quantities over rice. The split pea version is the classic; a different variety called gheymeh bademjan adds fried aubergine in place of the potato topping.
